_comment: Curated dead-code verdicts joined into the coverage report by
dead      — no caller anywhere in first-party code; delete.
test-only — only unit tests call it; relocate to test support.
gap       — (default for unmatched zero-hit fns) needs a test.
Every entry needs evidence a reviewer can check without rerunning
the analysis: the caller search that proved it, or the design
invariant (with doc citation) that makes the path unreachable.
Entries match by file prefix + substring of the (de)mangled name.

verdicts.evidence: google.protobuf.Struct fields peel to map<string, dyn>; RejectDyn refuses dyn before codegen, so no checked program reaches the unpack. Unlock = dyn passthrough (PROPOSALS-scale change).
google.protobuf.ListValue peels to list<dyn>; RejectDyn refuses dyn before codegen. Unlock = dyn passthrough.
Dispatcher over the two dyn-typed JSON peels above; same RejectDyn gate.
Double map keys are checker-rejected in the static subset (langdef: map keys are int|uint|bool|string); arm is a tripwire for codegen drift.
Only caller is the checker-rejected double-key arm above.
Comprehension prologue pre-checks CEL_ERROR/CEL_UNKNOWN before vending a view; fires only on codegen drift. Miscompile tripwire per CLAUDE.md.
Same prologue pre-check as vend_poison_list_view; codegen-drift tripwire.
Engine-side trap conversion: reachable only on codegen/runtime drift (kernel poisons instead of trapping on every legal path). Tripwire, keep.
Runtime kernel poisons instead of trapping on every reachable path; a trap means codegen/runtime drift. Tripwire, keep.

Strict dispatch absorbs CEL_UNKNOWN args before the callback runs (same 3VL family as DecodeWireError); pinned by e2e HostFnTest.UnknownValuedArgContract. Unlock = a non-strict-functions AddFunction API.
3VL absorbs error-valued args before host-fn dispatch, so a wire error can't reach ArgValue decode; pinned by e2e HostFnTest.ErrorValuedArgContract. Unlock = a non-strict-functions AddFunction API.
Called only from native kernel unit tests (cel_make_test, cel_compare_test); no codegen emit site and no wasm-path caller.
Native kernel unit tests only; no codegen emit site, no wasm-path caller.
Native kernel unit tests only; no codegen emit site, no wasm-path caller.
Native kernel unit tests only; no codegen emit site, no wasm-path caller.
Native kernel unit tests only; no codegen emit site, no wasm-path caller.
Host-reentry export consumed by native tests; the engine allocator uses arena_alloc/arena_reset. Relocation candidate.
Same as arena_cursor.
Native tests only; wasm build answers size via memory.size intrinsic path.
Native tests only; alias surface of cel_memory_size_.
Sole caller TypeFromCelType dispatches composites (message/list/map/optional) before this scalar mapping; the uncovered arms are the composite/kUnknown case-breaks + the ABSL_CHECK(false) tripwire.

Uncovered arms are kOptional + kUnknown only.  No decl surface spells optional: parse_and_check.cc TypeParser has no optional production, and function_library.cc rejects optional<T> params/returns; kUnknown is the ABSL_CHECK tripwire for the default-constructed sentinel.

Uncovered lines are the kCelDefined ABSL_CHECK(false) arm — kCelDefined decls import under per-module aliases and never produce a cel_fn wire row; the CEL-defined backend itself was deleted 2026-07-27.
Uncovered lines in the FSM are the unreachable-state ABSL_CHECK(false) in Step (the State enum is closed and every value has a case).

The checker admits only index_list(list(A), int) — codegen can emit CEL_INT (or absorbed error/unknown) indexes exclusively; the CEL_UINT / CEL_DOUBLE / kind-mismatch arms guard the wire against a codegen regression.  Verified: ListAtCallTarget in expr_lower.cc is the only emit family, and no uint/double list-index overload exists in the static subset.

The uncovered lines are the unchecked-AST FailedPrecondition guard; ParseAndCheck always checks before calling RejectDyn, so the arm is an internal-contract tripwire (unit-covered in parse_and_check_test).

Uncovered lines are the kType/kOptional ABSL_CHECK tripwire — guarded upstream by ValidateDeclTypesMappable (compiler.cc), which rejects such decls at Build with a diagnostic (e2e: host_fn_test DeclDiagnosticsE2ETest).
Remaining uncovered lines are the UNSPECIFIED/unhandled ABSL_CHECK tripwires; every name arm is e2e-covered by type_value_test's ident grid.
Remaining uncovered lines are the UNSPECIFIED/unhandled ABSL_CHECK tripwires; the six wrapper-name arms are e2e-covered by type_value_test's WrapperBool..WrapperBytes ident rows.
Remaining uncovered lines are the UNSPECIFIED/unhandled ABSL_CHECK tripwires; Any/Timestamp/Duration name arms are e2e-covered by type_value_test ident rows and any_test.
Uncovered lines are wasmtime engine/config creation failures (wasmtime_config_new / wasmtime_engine_new returning null, config-set errors) — allocator-failure arms with no e2e trigger.
Uncovered lines are `wasmtime_store_new returned null` / `wasi_config_new returned null` (allocator failure) and the context_set_wasi error arm; none reachable without fault injection.
Uncovered lines are wasmtime linker define/allocation failures; the success path is exercised by every planned instance.

Uncovered arms fire only if cel_runtime.wasm lacks a `memory` export or exports it non-shared.  That artifact is built by //runtime with the shared-memory linkopts, so the arms are tripwires against a corrupted / mismatched runtime build.
Uncovered arms are wasmtime linker-define failures plus `export missing from the runtime instance` — same corrupted-artifact tripwire as GetRuntimeMemoryExport.
Uncovered lines propagate BindRuntimeExport's tripwire status; the enumerated export list comes from the runtime catalogue we generate.
Uncovered lines are wasmtime linker-define failure propagation.

Uncovered arms require cel_runtime.wasm to be missing `arena_alloc` / `malloc`, to export them as non-functions, or with a non-all-i32 signature.  All three contradict how //runtime builds the artifact.
Uncovered arms require a missing / mistyped `arena_init` export, or a wasmtime call error / guest trap from it — the runtime's arena_init is a leaf that cannot trap under a correct build.

Uncovered lines are ABSL_CHECK tripwires on the runtime's memory layout (shared-memory size, __heap_base kind/value).  By construction of the runtime build; a violation is a build regression, not an input.
Uncovered lines are export-lookup failures on the statically-linked module, whose exports codegen itself emits.
Uncovered lines are wasmtime instantiate error / trap arms for cel_runtime.wasm — a fixed, validated artifact.

Uncovered arms require the expr module to lack an `eval` export, export it as a non-function, or with the wrong signature.  expr_lower always emits `$eval` with the pinned signature (WAT traces + module validation gate it).

Uncovered lines are arity / arg-kind mismatch arms on the wasm->host boundary; the call shape is emitted by codegen against the same decl the host registered, so a mismatch is a codegen regression tripwire.
Same as HostCallbackTrampoline for the plugin path: uncovered lines are the arity / lift / lower failure arms guarding a codegen-emitted call shape.
Uncovered lines are wasmtime linker-define failures during callback registration.
Uncovered lines are the per-arg lift failure propagation arm; the successful lifts for every supported carrier are covered by demo_plugin_e2e_test's KindMatrixEchoRoundTrips.

Uncovered remainder is defensive only: the wrong-kind guard (the runtime helper already routes on kind — the comment says so), the ExternrefTable miss (`a host-adapter bug`), and the non-proto-backing arm.  The happy path (type(msg) -> FQN) is e2e-covered by type_value_test.

Uncovered remainder is the type_id-out-of-range guard, the null-descriptor arm (FQN unresolvable at Plan time), the null-prototype arm (dynamic descriptors, a documented follow-up), and prototype->New() returning null (allocator failure).  The construction happy path is e2e-covered by proto_literal_test / wkt_field_set_test.

Uncovered remainder is the ExternrefTable-miss FailedPrecondition and the out-of-enum CompareProtoMessages CHECK; the equal / unequal / not-comparable outcomes are e2e-covered by arena_message_aggregate_eq_test.

Uncovered remainder guards a checker regression: a `Foo{...}` literal must construct a fresh OwnedProtoBacking, so a host-bound (immutable) ProtoBacking reaching the set path is a pipeline bug, not user input — the dynamic_cast mismatch arm says so in place.

Uncovered remainder is unreachable by construction, and each arm documents why in place: backings never return unknowns (operand-pair propagation runs first), aggregate kinds route through EncodeFieldResult / EncodeAggregateIfAny rather than the inline path, and type(x) lowers to the cel_type_of_at_v runtime helper instead of a Layer-1 backing call.

Uncovered remainder is kind/descriptor-mismatch rejects on a nested message field; the checker types `Foo{nested: Bar{...}}` before codegen emits the set, so reaching them means a codegen regression.  The success path is e2e-covered by wkt_field_set_test's nested-message rows.

Uncovered remainder is the non-CEL_MESSAGE kind guard, the ExternrefTable miss, the null-message arm, and the WKT-descriptor-mismatch arm whose own comment says `codegen only emits this for matching s.name()`.  Codegen emits the call only immediately after cel_make_message for a Timestamp/Duration literal; the 3VL absorb arm is e2e-covered by partial_eval_test's TimeUnwrapError row. Downgraded from by-design: the guards are reachable by driving the trampoline directly with a staged CelValue, and cel_host_test now does so, so exempting them from the tests metric was too generous.

Same shape as CelWktUnwrapTimeImpl, plus the produced-kind vs wrapper_kind cross-check the code labels in place as a `codegen-regression tripwire`.  The absorb arm is e2e-covered by partial_eval_test's WrapperUnwrapError rows. Downgraded from by-design: the guards are reachable by driving the trampoline directly with a staged CelValue, and cel_host_test now does so, so exempting them from the tests metric was too generous.

Uncovered remainder is per-cpp_type kind mismatch on a WKT wrapper's inner `value` field, plus the unexpected-inner-cpp_type CHECK.  The checker types `Int32Value{value: x}` before codegen emits the set, so a mismatch is a pipeline regression.
Same as SetWrapperInnerValue for the bool/int32/int64/uint32/uint64 arms; the range-check paths are e2e-covered by wkt_field_set_test's WrapperNarrowingRangeErrors.
Uncovered remainder is the BYTES / STRING / ENUM kind-mismatch rejects.  Field type comes from the descriptor and the value's type from the checker, so disagreement is a codegen regression.
Uncovered remainder is descriptor-pool misses (inner FQN absent, no generated prototype) and a wrapper lacking its `value` field — all InternalError arms over the generated pool's own contents.
Uncovered remainder guards a repeated-message element that is not CEL_MESSAGE, has no externref entry, or whose backing carries no proto message — each a host-adapter invariant, not user input.
Same guards as AppendRepeatedMessage on the host-list path, plus the unknown-cpp_type CHECK.

Uncovered remainder is the non-CEL_MAP_HOST kind guard (codegen routes only host-origin maps here; literal maps use the arena kernel), the ExternrefTable miss, and the DecodeKey failure — the absorb arm is e2e-covered by partial_eval_test's MapIn rows.

Uncovered remainder is the kMessageJson arm plus the unreachable scalar/map/repeated cases and their CHECK.  The JSON arm cannot be reached from e2e AT ALL: a google.protobuf.Struct field types as map(string, dyn) and a Value field as dyn, and RejectDyn refuses both before codegen — so it is e2e-unreachable by construction while remaining unit-reachable through cel_host_test.  The plain-message, wrapper and temporal arms are e2e-covered.

Uncovered remainder rejects a component value that is not a 2-field {seconds,nanos} record.  wit-bindgen generates that record from the WIT our own emitter wrote, so a mismatch is a generator regression — see doc/design/10-plugin-wit-pipeline.md §3.

Uncovered remainder is the illegal-map-key-kind reject (FunctionLibrary::Builder rejects those at decl time), the non-list valkind guard, and the non-tuple-entry guard — all over a shape wit-bindgen produced from our own WIT.

Uncovered remainder is the per-kind CelfnVsValueMismatch arms: the declared CelType and the runtime Value disagreeing.  The checker types every plugin call site against the same decl, so a mismatch is a pipeline regression.  Every supported carrier's success path is e2e-covered by demo_plugin_e2e_test's KindMatrixEchoRoundTrips.
Uncovered remainder is the optional<T> and type-of-types return-shape rejects (both refused at decl time by FunctionLibrary::Builder) and the kUnknown invariant arm.
Uncovered remainder is the non-list valkind guard, the missing-generated-prototype InternalError (its message names the fix: link the cc_proto_library), and the parse-failure arm.
Uncovered remainder is the kind mismatch and the non-proto-backed-message reject (a custom HostMessageBacking cannot be serialised).
Uncovered remainder is the externref-miss and null-proto-message guards on a CEL_MESSAGE the runtime itself produced — host-adapter invariants.
Uncovered remainder is the impossible-id-count guard and propagation arms over a CEL_UNKNOWN descriptor the runtime wrote; malformed wire bytes there are an invariant break, not user input.
Uncovered remainder is the kNone-storage ABSL_CHECK: the producing visitor must set storage before this call, so reaching it is a LayoutPass regression.
Uncovered remainder is the unsupported-operand-repr CHECK over a closed set; parse_and_check.cc UnacceptableLabel rejects every other shape before codegen, as the message says in place.
Uncovered lines are `return s;` propagation arms for cel-cpp checker-library registration failures — each library is a compile-time constant of ours, so a failure is a vendored-dep regression.
Same shape: propagation arms for macro registration failures over a fixed macro set.
Same shape: propagation arms over fixed checker configuration.
Uncovered remainder is the externref-miss and null-proto-message guards on a CEL_MESSAGE the runtime produced — host-adapter invariants, mirroring instance.cc DecodeHostMessageAt.

Uncovered remainder is the per-cpp_type ScalarKindMismatch rejects; the checker types the field expression against the descriptor before codegen emits the set, so a mismatch is a pipeline regression.  The int32/uint32 range paths are e2e-covered by wkt_field_set_test.

Uncovered remainder is the kEnum / kUnknown UnimplementedError arms — the CLAUDE.md `stub until <milestone>` form, deliberately loud — plus the kNull encoder, which no declared variable can reach because CelType::IsDeclarableAsVariable rejects kNull outright.
Uncovered remainder rejects a comprehension whose iter_range is neither list nor map; the checker constrains comprehension ranges to those two before codegen runs.
Uncovered remainder is the empty-overload_id UnimplementedError, whose message names its own cause: ResolvePass left the annotation unstamped, i.e. a pipeline regression.

Uncovered remainder is the null-reflection InternalError, the cord-backed-scratch branch (reflection materialising a string into the caller's scratch, which generated-message storage does not do), and the unhandled-cpp_type arm.

Uncovered remainder is the ResourceExhausted arm for a static region past the reserved low-memory window.  The limit itself is pinned in e2e/limits_test.cc per the compilation-limits rule; this is the internal assertion behind it.

Uncovered remainder is the non-UNKNOWN-operand poison (codegen emits the merge only for two unknowns) and the empty-UnknownSet arms, which the function's own comment rules out: `Every production writer (host trampolines, activation marshal, host-fn returns) mints a non-empty descriptor, so an empty side reaches here only from hand-built fixtures`.

Uncovered remainder is the LIST-side unknown/error absorb: an arena list is materialised by the same expression that indexes it, so the list operand is never 3VL.  The INDEX-side absorb is e2e-covered by partial_eval_test's ArenaListAt rows.

Uncovered remainder is the bytes / null / duration / timestamp / IP arms.  Every caller is a map-key lookup (cel_map_index.c:90,128 and cel_runtime.c:129,179,224), and langdef restricts map keys to bool/int/uint/string, so no legal program can present those kinds here.  The kernel is written generically; the callers are not.

Uncovered remainder is the non-literal map-entry ABSL_CHECK, in both the plain and conditional arms.  Its own message names the missing piece — `needs runtime map-merge helper` — i.e. the CLAUDE.md stub-until-a-later-milestone form, deliberately loud rather than silently wrong.

Uncovered remainder rejects an iter_range whose storage kind is kNone; the accepted set (kWorkspaceSlot, kStaticRodata, kLocal) is spelled in the message, and LayoutPass assigns one of those before codegen runs.
Uncovered remainder is guest malloc failure — wasmtime error, guest trap, and a NULL return.  Allocator-exhaustion arms with no e2e trigger.
Uncovered remainder is the host-string-arena OOM arm; the kind-mismatch arm is reachable and is covered by the activation-boundary suite.
Uncovered remainder is the non-string operand poison — the checker types ip()'s argument — and the CEL_ERR_OVERFLOW arm, which fires only on arena exhaustion.
Same pair: a non-IP operand cannot reach a checker-typed string(ip) call, and OVERFLOW is arena exhaustion.
Same pair for cidr().
Same pair for string(cidr).
Uncovered remainder is the operand-kind poison and the INVALID_ARGUMENT arm for a malformed pair; both operands are checker-typed.
Uncovered remainder is the non-optional operand poison on both sides; optional.or() is checker-typed to optional operands.
Uncovered remainder is the closed-dispatch __builtin_trap and the type-mismatch poison behind it — the caller routes only the kinds the switch enumerates.

Uncovered remainder is the arena-OOM early return and the closed-dispatch __builtin_trap.  The CEL_LIST_HOST / CEL_MAP_HOST probe arms are now e2e-covered by optional_test's OfNonZeroValueHostBacked rows.

Uncovered remainder across the conversion kernels is the operand-kind poison: int()/uint()/double()/string()/bytes() are checker-typed, so a wrong-kind operand is a codegen regression rather than user input.  The conversions' value paths and their range/parse errors are e2e-covered by conversion_test.

Uncovered remainder is the CEL_TYPE arm and the unknown-kind default.  A host fn cannot declare a `type` parameter — function_library.cc's ExtractType has no `type` keyword and Build() rejects the kind — so no call can present one; the default guards the closed wire vocabulary.
Uncovered remainder is the truncated-arena-header and missing-externref guards over a CelValue the runtime itself wrote.
Uncovered remainder is the missing-generated_factory-prototype and missing-value-field InternalErrors, both over the generated descriptor pool's own contents for a WKT wrapper.

Uncovered remainder is the non-CEL_LIST_HOST kind guard (codegen routes only host-origin lists here; literal lists use the arena kernel) and the ExternrefTable miss.  The absorb arm is e2e-covered by partial_eval_test's ListSize row.
Same shape as CelListSizeImpl for maps; the absorb arm is covered by the MapSize row.

Uncovered remainder is the field_ref_id-out-of-range and field-not-found-on-descriptor guards.  Both ids come from the cel.abi table the compiler emitted against the same descriptor, so a miss is a pipeline regression.  The 3VL absorb and range-poison paths are e2e-covered.

Uncovered remainder is the export-is-not-a-function guard and the linker define failure.  Engine::Use already validates the component's export surface against the decls before Plan binds them (CheckPluginExportsStatically), so a mismatch here is a validation regression.
Uncovered remainder is the missing-interface guard, over the same pre-validated export surface.
Uncovered remainder is wasmtime_component_linker_new returning null and the delete-on-error path — allocator-failure arms.

Uncovered remainder is the ForEach-over-visits-Size InternalError: it fires only if a HostMapBacking's ForEach disagrees with its own Size(), which is a backing-implementation invariant, not user input.

Uncovered remainder is the empty-UnknownSet fast path and the arena-OOM arm.  Per cel_unknown_merge's comment every production writer mints a non-empty descriptor, so the empty case reaches here only from hand-built fixtures.
Uncovered remainder is key/value decode-failure propagation out of the ForEach lambda, over entries the backing itself produced.
Uncovered remainder is the non-message value-kind reject and the missing-backing arm for a map<K, message> entry; the checker types the entry value before codegen emits the insert.
Uncovered remainder in ProtoList::At is the cord-backed-scratch string branch and the unhandled-cpp_type InternalError over a closed descriptor enum.
Uncovered remainder is guest malloc failure during activation marshalling — wasmtime error, guest trap, and NULL return.  Allocator-exhaustion arms.

Uncovered remainder is the wrong-kind `poison(out, CEL_ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH)` guard: a type-checked CEL expression cannot deliver a mismatched kind to a conversion kernel, so the arm is a codegen-regression tripwire.  runtime/cel_convert_test.cc DOES cover it natively (e.g. UintToIntKindMismatch), but runtime/* rows in this report come from the wasm gcov layer alone -- runtime/ is not in native_cov_report.py's DEFAULT_SCOPES -- so native kernel tests cannot score here.  test-only rather than by-design precisely because a unit test does exercise it.

Uncovered remainder is this kernel's two guards. (1) The wrong-kind `poison(out, CEL_ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH)` arm: a type-checked expression cannot reach it because the checker fixes the operand kinds for every net-ext overload, and runtime/cel_net_ext_test.cc DOES cover it natively (7 TYPE_MISMATCH assertions) -- but runtime/* rows here come from the wasm gcov layer alone (runtime/ is not in native_cov_report.py's DEFAULT_SCOPES), so that native coverage cannot score. (2) The `poison(out, CEL_ERR_OVERFLOW)` arm, taken only when the per-Eval arena cannot fit the result: this one is covered by NOTHING today -- no e2e row and no unit test -- and reaching it needs arena exhaustion, so it is an open gap rather than a satisfied one. Happy paths are e2e-covered by e2e/network_ext_test.cc. test-only, not by-design, because arm (1) is genuinely unit-exercised.

Uncovered remainder is this kernel's two guards. (1) The wrong-kind `poison(out, CEL_ERR_TYPE_MISMATCH)` arm: a type-checked expression cannot reach it because the checker fixes the operand kinds for every net-ext overload, and runtime/cel_net_ext_test.cc DOES cover it natively (7 TYPE_MISMATCH assertions) -- but runtime/* rows here come from the wasm gcov layer alone (runtime/ is not in native_cov_report.py's DEFAULT_SCOPES), so that native coverage cannot score. (2) The `poison(out, CEL_ERR_OVERFLOW)` arm, taken only when the per-Eval arena cannot fit the result: this one is covered by NOTHING today -- no e2e row and no unit test -- and reaching it needs arena exhaustion, so it is an open gap rather than a satisfied one.
